Klyachanovo Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kliachanovo, Ukraine

Not demolished. Presumably established in the 19th century, this cemetery existed by 1840 per epigraphic data, presumably used until WWII, though its latest preserved gravestone dates to 1930. Jews are believed to have arrived in the mid-18th century; three Jewish families lived there by 1768, growing to 55 by 1830 and 187 (of 703 total residents) by 1880, then rising to 215 by 1921 (Czechoslovak period). Jews were engaged in agriculture and commerce, owning two quarries. Hungarian forces arrived March 1939, persecuting Jews and forcing them from their occupations; area Jews were drafted into forced labor battalions, with others sent to the Eastern Front where most perished. Some families without Hungarian citizenship were expelled to Kamianets-Podilskyi and murdered; remaining Kliachanovo Jews were deported to Auschwitz in late May 1944. No Jews live in the town today.
